subject: Recap & recommended route for Bright Analytics inference deployment
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@brightanalytics.com>, Elliot Grant <elliot@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Bright Analytics inference requirements & next steps

Hi Samira / Elliot —

Great call today — appreciate the deep dive. Quick recap of the core requirements we heard:
- P95 end-to-end latency target: ~75ms for short prompts (~120 tokens typical).
- Sustained throughput target: ~150 inference requests/sec during business hours, with spikes to ~300 r/s for short windows.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC isolation for production data; encryption-in-transit and at-rest.
- Data residency: US regions only for this initial rollout.

Options we discussed (high-level):
1) Hosted API: fastest onboarding, shared multi-tenant serving with prefix/KV caching and aggressive batching. Pros: <2 weeks to production, built-in monitoring, predictable dev experience. Cons: networking adds to measured end-to-end latency; very large sustained throughput may raise cost unless we tune batching and caching aggressively.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): provisioned GPUs for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale; can hit strict latency SLOs by sizing and pinning instances. Pros: better fit for sustained 150 r/s + bursty 300 r/s patterns and tighter tail latency. Cons: procurement lead time for reserved capacity and commitment required.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended for regulated workloads where control plane isolation and on-prem hardware are mandatory. More involved timeline.

Suggested next steps (for us + Bright Analytics):
- Connor / Redwood: run a short synthetic load run (we create a test harness simulating your token distribution and p95 target) — estimate 2 business days to prepare.
- Bright: confirm exact token distribution for top-10 call patterns (we need sample prompts and average token counts).
- Send security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence (we attached our responses in this thread).
- Align on pilot scope: 30-day Dedicated pilot vs Hosted POC (we can price both options).

I'll pull together a recommendation and cost delta once we get the sample prompts and agree the measurement point for latency (edge → app server → Redwood response).

Attachments: Bright_Analytics_QoS_Slides.pdf (we captured the call metrics), BA_Security_Questionnaire_responses.pdf

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@brightanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Grant <elliot@brightanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Bright Analytics inference requirements & next steps

Thanks, Connor — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Our 75ms p95 constraint is end-to-end (our front-end load balancer → backend → Redwood inference → back to client). Network hops are non-negligible; we'd like Redwood to target ~50ms server-side p95 if we go Hosted.
- Typical prompt length is 100–140 tokens; the long-tail (rare) is up to ~600 tokens but those can be served asynchronously.
- On cost: can you provide a rough delta (order-of-magnitude) between Hosted and Dedicated for our expected profile (150 sustained / 300 burst)? Even ballpark is fine for internal budgeting.

We attached the internal QoS doc we referenced in the call (see attachment stub). Happy to jump on a short call next week after you send the test harness.

—Samira
Samira Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure, Bright Analytics
samira.patel@brightanalytics.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommendation for Bright Analytics (confidential)

Connor / Marissa —

Quick internal note before we send the external recommendation: based on the numbers (150 sustained, 300 burst, and 50ms server-side p95 target if Hosted), my read is: Dedicated reserved capacity is the higher-probability path to meet their SLOs and economics. Rationale: predictable per-token unit cost at scale, ability to pre-warm KV cache and tune kernel selection for their sequence distribution, and easier isolation for their compliance asks.

Proposal for engagement:
- Offer a 30-day Dedicated pilot (3x midsize GPUs) with monitoring and a migration playbook; include a 30% pilot credit to remove procurement friction.
- Alternatively, offer a Hosted POC with strict test harness and a defined escalation to Dedicated if p95 cannot be achieved at the tested traffic levels.
- Commercial: recommend a 10% introductory discount on committed months if they convert post-pilot within 60 days.

If you agree, I'll draft the external note and price examples for both pilots. Also recommend we prepare a short performance-run plan (load scripts + gating criteria) so the pilot has measurable acceptance.

-L
Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Sales Operations

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Recommendation & next steps: Dedicated pilot for Bright Analytics

Hi Samira / Elliot —

Following internal alignment, our recommended route is to run a 30-day Dedicated pilot scoped as follows:
- Capacity: 3 x a40-equivalent GPUs (provisioned, reserved for pilot window) with autoscaling to add 1x on sustained >250 r/s for >10m.
- Acceptance criteria: server-side p95 <= 50ms for the top-10 call patterns at sustained 150 r/s; end-to-end p95 target of <=75ms measured from your edge (we'll instrument both sides).
- Security & compliance: pilot runs in our US production region with VPC peering; we'll enable encryption & provide SOC2 artifacts (attached).
- Commercials (pilot): 30-day pilot, 30% credit applied to the pilot invoice; 10% conversion discount if they commit to a 6+ month reserved plan within 60 days post-pilot. Exact numbers below (ballpark):
  - Hosted POC estimate: ~$8k–$12k / month for the test profile (higher per-token),
  - Dedicated pilot (provisional reserved pricing): ~$20k/month list, net after pilot credit TBD — we'll provide line-item pricing when you confirm scope.

Next steps from here:
1) Samira / Elliot: confirm you want to proceed with Dedicated pilot and share the top-10 prompt set and any production traffic traces we can use (anonymized).
2) Connor / Redwood: create test harness + load script and propose pilot start dates (we can be ready in ~7 business days after scope sign-off).
3) Legal / Procurement: we'll send a short pilot agreement (DocuSign) and a HubSpot trial record (links below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123
HubSpot trial: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

If you're aligned, I'll queue the pilot agreement and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks all — looking forward to running this with your team.

—Connor
